A 2024 start can only appear here if it has already finished, so recent
cohorts are a sample of their own fastest members. The slow half has not
arrived. It is a race timed only on the people who crossed the line.

share reaching primary completion, by phase — starts 2010–2018
Phase 1 finishes fastest and phase 2 slowest, at every
horizon. Phase 3 runs four times larger than phase 2 by median
enrollment and still finishes more often — so the phase-2
delay is not size. Bars are 1, 3 and 5 years.
and trials did not get bigger
Median actual enrollment is 57 participants in every start
year from 2008 to 2022, and the 90th percentile drifted down.
Whatever is slower, it is not more participants.
ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, fetched 2026-09-22; start date from the second walk. 449,259 interventional trials with a start date. A trial counts as
finished only on an ACTUAL primary completion date, so an estimated one is treated as not yet finished. Cohorts are only drawn where at least 300
trials have had the full window to finish in. This measures duration, not difficulty: a longer trial may be a larger question or a harder population.
